html:
A Chinese Buddhist monk of the Tang dynasty, known in Japan as Ganjin, who reached Japan in 753 and founded the temple of Tōshōdai-ji in Nara.

He was a respected master of the monastic rules at Yangzhou. In 742 two Japanese monks asked him to come to Japan, which had no proper way to ordain monks. Between 743 and 753 he tried to cross six times. Storms, shipwreck and officials who did not want him to leave stopped the first five. On one attempt he was blown as far as Hainan. He lost his sight along the way.

In Nara he set up an ordination platform at Tōdai-ji and ordained the retired emperor Shōmu. He also brought knowledge of medicine and art. A lacquer portrait statue of him, made around the time of his death, is kept at Tōshōdai-ji and is one of Japan's great treasures. His story is a classic of the Tang and Japan exchange.
